STEP 1 - Vessel type: The food sits on a large white square plate with a flat centre and a raised rim band. No inner wall or bowl shadow is visible, so this is a flat plate (square).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type cue: square plates are typically 20-30 cm. The plate fills much of the frame, so it looks medium-large, about 26 cm across.
b) Reference cue: the food cluster is roughly 9-10 cm wide, and it occupies about a third of the plate width. That implies the plate is about 26-28 cm across.
Reconciled width: about 27 cm square, so area is about 729 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items on the plate:
- Food footprint: the cluster covers roughly 15-18% of the plate area, or about 120 cm².
- Thickness: the beef and greens form a mound about 2 pieces deep at the thickest point. Each piece is about 1 cm thick, so the peak is about 2 cm and the average is about 1 cm.
- Volume: 120 cm² x 1 cm = about 120 ml.
- Meat-and-greens mixture bulk density is about 0.9 g/ml, since it is mostly cooked meat with some cooked greens. That gives about 110 g.
- Split: beef stir-fry with sauce and cooked leafy greens, plus a little rice or aromatics underneath.
  - Beef (cooked, stir-fried, about 75%): about 80 g.
  - Cooked leafy greens (basil or similar, about 15%): about 20 g.
  - Sauce and oil (about 10%): about 10 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: there is no clearly visible rice base, though some grain bits appear among the meat. I add about 15 g of rice as a hidden base.

STEP 5 - Energy per 100 g (cooked):
- Beef stir-fry meat: about 220 kcal/100 g.
- Cooked leafy greens: about 35 kcal/100 g.
- Sauce and oil: about 120 kcal/100 g.
- Cooked rice: about 130 kcal/100 g.

Total weight is about 125 g, with roughly 290 kcal.
